question.text: Fund MAS (Cat III) takes these positions after a merger announcement: Buy 1 lakh shares of ACQ at INR 540 (invest INR 5.40 cr) and Buy 10 lakh shares of TGT at INR 39.25 (invest INR 3.925 cr). By EOD, ACQ closes at INR 567.80 and TGT closes at INR 41.10. What is the 1-day ROI?

explanation.text: The Logic: ACQ value = 1,00,000 * 567.80 = INR 5.678 cr. TGT value = 10,00,000 * 41.10 = INR 4.10 cr. Total value = INR 9.778 cr. Total invested = 5.40 + 3.925 = INR 9.325 cr. ROI = (9.778 - 9.325) / 9.325 = 0.453/9.325 = 4.86% (PDF Example 10.7). The Trap: Option B uses only one leg. Option C forgets to net against investment. Option D compounds errors. Note: Example 10.7 in the workbook walks through this exact merger-arbitrage ROI calculation.
